gates.reason: Reviewed prospectus discloses related borrowing, interest and remuneration; no substantiated severe diversion or minority abuse was identified. Related demand borrowing and concentrated ownership economics remain risks, not proof of misconduct.
Restated same-scope statements and the reported cash bridge support a usable baseline. FY26 margin durability is tested in the model; it is not itself an accounting failure.

IPO-adjusted funds support planned machinery and repayment. Ordinary bear case needs no material rescue equity; demand-loan repayment is explicitly stressed. Severe combined demand, margin, working-capital and capex stress requires financing that is not assured, so downside resilience is low.

Official October 19 trades and eligible SM series corroborate trading. Recent listing allows only shorter history; a ₹5 lakh reference equals 3.12 lots and three whole lots cost ₹481,500. Limited PAN breadth, lock-ins and absent live depth require caution. No claim of guaranteed execution.

sections.text: Completed conditional review: BQS 5.02, growth-quality GQS 4.20, IAS 3.21. Central return is 4.8%, below the 15% research hurdle. Historical strengths do not remove concentration, capital-allocation, funding or liquidity risks. This is a watchlist assessment, not a buy recommendation. [S1, S2, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026. The final prospectus provides restated standalone FY24–FY26 financials. NSE admission circular CML76205 confirms listing on September 7, 2026 and 21,874,800 shares. The official October 19 close was ₹133.75 with a 1,200-share lot. The decoded SM row is eligible; status 6 means price discovery, not suspension. These are dated facts, not live execution guarantees. [S1,S2,M1,M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical quality factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 2, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 7, BAL 5, EXEC 6 and EARN 5. BQS is 5.02 and GQS is 4.20. IAS factors are R 2, D 3, P 3 and L 7; exact weighted arithmetic is retained in the score audit. All factor confidence is Medium. The investment assessment uses a normalized central case, not a probability-weighted forecast.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Technical yarn manufacturer including para-aramid, polypropylene, modacrylic and flame-retardant viscose products. Single leased Petlad, Gujarat facility creates location and legal-tenure dependency. Customers can specify approved raw-material suppliers. [S1]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Product qualification could support switching friction, but the ten largest customers accounted for 68.85% of FY26 revenue and contracts are not long-term. Specialization alone is not proven pricing power. [S1]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue FY24/FY25/FY26 was ₹109.87/114.03/117.37 crore, a calculated two-year CAGR of about 3.36%. Synthetic-yarn output rose from 2,809 to 3,247 to 3,619 MT; polypropylene output stayed broadly flat at 680/653/656 MT. Physical volume evidence is materially stronger than reported revenue growth, but price/mix attribution is unresolved. [S1]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Synthetic-yarn utilization reached 96.51%; polypropylene utilization was 63.95%. The IPO funds ₹25.5083 crore machinery and proposes synthetic capacity rising from 3,750 to 5,000 MT, while polypropylene remains 1,025 MT. FY24–FY26 incremental NOPAT/invested-capital proxy is 26.3%, including CWIP, but reversion to FY25 operating margin reduces it to 3.1%. CAP 5 reflects this dependence on margin gains, not a verified project IRR. The modeled 5% annual synthetic-volume assumption reaches about 4,619 MT in year five, within planned capacity, but demand and commissioning remain assumptions. [S1]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Related-party transactions totaled ₹15.8865 crore in FY26 versus ₹23.6512 crore in FY25. Related unsecured loans were ₹18.428 crore: ₹10.878 crore repayable on demand and ₹7.55 crore after six years, with applicable interest of 10–12%. Director remuneration rose from ₹1.02 crore to ₹1.32 crore. These disclosed economic exposures justify monitoring without implying diversion. The ten-year manufacturing lease from 2023 creates tenure dependence for new capex. Initial allotment promoter holding was 43.05%; aggregate lock-ins included substantial public holdings, so public ownership is not executable float. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: Three-year CFO sums ₹38.3011 crore against PAT ₹31.6009 crore: calculated cumulative CFO/PAT 1.212. Cash capex totals ₹44.4526 crore, so cumulative CFO less capex is negative ₹6.1515 crore. Net working capital rose to 35.66% of sales from 28.33% FY24. FY26 materials consumed fell to ₹64.6757 crore from ₹69.7359 crore, purchased traded stock fell from ₹2.9337 crore to zero and other expense fell ₹19.3590 to ₹17.0993 crore. These explain substantial profit uplift without equivalent sales growth; persistence remains open. [S1] MD&A quantifies ₹2.6028 crore lower power/fuel expense, alongside ₹5.0602 crore lower materials and disappearance of ₹2.9337 crore traded purchases. Captive solar includes a 380 kW rooftop facility and commissioned 4 MW leased-land plant. These offer plausible cost explanations, but do not prove recurring yield improvement; inventory capitalization and product mix must also be traced. [S1, pp 255–256] Opening income-tax provision ₹1.1264 crore and accrued interest ₹0.0440 crore are conservatively settled before the first modeled year. Employee bonus/gratuity and expense provisions totaling ₹0.9141 crore are included in operating liabilities, reducing opening operating working capital to ₹43.0244 crore. Future-year taxes and interest are separate, so the opening claims are not duplicated. [S1] Opening-claim audit: operating statutory, payroll and expense liabilities of ₹1.0583 crore and current employee/expense provisions of ₹0.9141 crore are already included in opening and forecast operating WC. They are not charged again as separate debt. Opening tax/interest settlement remains ₹1.1704 crore. No separate noncurrent employee obligation is reported in the opening balance sheet. The ₹5.4554 crore opening deferred-tax liability is separately reserved once at terminal. Forecast tax at 25.17% of future positive PBT does not model legacy tax-basis reversals; this reserve is a conservative timing assumption, not a cash tax currently due. Deferred-tax assets receive no cash credit. If legacy reversal is explicitly included in future cash taxes, this reserve must be released to avoid duplication. Existing bank principal remains in the debt schedule and terminal debt; no duplicate current-maturity deduction is made. [S1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Corrected actual-opening model includes all identified opening tax, interest and operating provision claims. Bear/base/bull conditional IRRs are -17.6%/4.8%/24.6%. Central five-year assumptions and annual cash, debt and dilution schedules are in the valuation model. At central operating performance, a 15% hurdle requires approximately 19.4 times terminal EV/EBIT. The prior optimistic case remains separately labeled. Opening income-tax provision ₹1.1264 crore and accrued interest ₹0.0440 crore are conservatively settled before the first modeled year. Employee bonus/gratuity and expense provisions totaling ₹0.9141 crore are included in operating liabilities, reducing opening operating working capital to ₹43.0244 crore. Future-year taxes and interest are separate, so the opening claims are not duplicated. [S1, S2, M1] The terminal bridge additionally retains the audited legacy employee and deferred-tax claims; the annual operating and financing schedules are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Permanent-loss path: major customer withdrawal, weaker yarn pricing, leased-site disruption or a low-return capex cycle, compounded by working-capital intensity. Related demand loans could stress liquidity despite positive historical CFO. [S1]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged valuation and no dividends, 5× in five years requires 37.97% annual per-share growth and 10× requires 58.49%. Historical revenue CAGR near 3.36% does not establish either path. New machinery alone is not an earnings forecast.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Check first post-listing results, customer concentration, realised revenue per tonne, machinery commissioning, lease tenure, proceeds monitoring and debt repayment. Require cash conversion after expansion rather than extrapolating FY26 margins. Next-session NSE REG1 alerts, effective October 21,2026: Less than 100 unique PAN traded in previous 30 days; SME scrip is not regularly traded. These caution flags do not establish wrongdoing or actual missing trading sessions. [M_REG1, M_REG1_FORMAT]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed conditional review. This is a moderately rated business with weak measured revenue growth, a margin-normalization question and an unattractive central-case return at the stated price. A low IAS here reflects return and downside risk as well as implementation limits, not a claim that the business cannot grow. No transaction or position size is recommended.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Reviewed final prospectus risks, objects, restated accounts, related borrowing and capacity disclosures; admission and initial shareholding confirm listing and shares. Financial calculations retain actual opening balances. Remaining uncertainties are future machinery commissioning, realized product mix and margins, actual utilization of IPO proceeds and live execution depth. These are modeled and disclosed, not unresolved listing or allotment facts. The September 29 presentation repeats FY26 financials and the commissioned 380 kW rooftop and 4 MW captive solar assets; it provides no independently verified post-IPO machinery-utilization or revenue update. Its growth labels are not substituted for the underlying historical tables. [S3]

GOV.reason: Quantified related funding and remuneration, but demand-loan terms and issue costs require minority-alignment scrutiny; no substantiated abuse inferred.

MOAT.reason: Technical yarn specialization and high utilization support useful positioning; customer concentration and absent long contracts limit durable pricing-power evidence.

REV.reason: Select FY24–FY26 two-year comparable CAGR3.36% from three annual observations, because five-year comparable prospectus history is unavailable. Starting rubric 2; no adjustment. Higher production is contrary positive evidence but not verified equivalent sales realization.

DUR.reason: High synthetic utilization and specified machinery expansion support demand access; polypropylene spare capacity and concentrated customers prevent stronger runway rating.

CAP.reason: FY24–FY26 endpoint ΔNOPAT/ΔIC proxy 26.3%, with CWIP included, exceeds assumed 12–16% capital cost. However FY25-margin reversion reduces proxy to 3.1%; large solar/manufacturing capex and margin step-up make sustained incremental returns mixed rather than reliably exceptional.

CASH.reason: Cumulative CFO exceeds PAT across three annual periods, while capex and working-capital build consume funding. Strong conversion but not full-cycle 9–10 economics.

BAL.reason: Fresh IPO funds and debt-repayment allocation improve capacity; on-demand related debt and working-capital growth leave stress sensitivity. Do not assume repayment completed.

EXEC.reason: Higher production/utilization and commissioned solar demonstrate execution. New machinery remains prospective and cost savings need sustained validation.

EARN.reason: Operating cost reductions support profit growth, but 88.53% PAT growth versus 2.93% sales and IPO dilution limit extrapolation. Strong one-year margin uplift is not equivalent to recurring per-share growth.

R.reason: Central conditional five-year IRR 4.84% after all identified opening claims is -10.16 percentage points below/above the 15% hurdle, mapping to R=1. Forecasts and terminal tax timing remain assumptions.

D.reason: Ordinary bear terminal equity loss is 61.9%. Severe combined operating and financing stress requires conditional rescue and can cause worse loss if financing fails. IPO cash supports ordinary operations, not the quoted equity value.

P.reason: Central operating performance requires approximately 19.4 times terminal EV/EBIT to earn the 15% hurdle, above the central exit assumption. Stronger growth, margin or rerating must bridge the gap; the prior optimistic scenario is not the central case.

L.reason: Recent 20-session conservative turnover implies 0.70 days at 5% participation, starting band 9. Downgraded to 7 for short post-IPO history, ₹160,500 lot granularity, less-than-100-PAN caution and substantial initial lock-ins; live spread/depth is not observed.

sensitivities.name: Working capital increases by 10% of sales
Immediate related demand-loan repayment in addition to IPO bank repayment
Operating margin returns to approximately FY25 level
Legacy deferred-tax reserve fully released without incremental cash tax: timing upper bound
sensitivities.interpretation: Alternative assumption only. Opening employee claim and all other claims remain deducted.

assumptions: All model money is in INR crore and shares in crore. March 2026 actual balances are bridged by the known IPO, not described as an observed October balance sheet. Five full operating years approximate October 2026 to October 2031.

Opening revenue ₹117.3714 crore, debt ₹47.9245 crore, cash ₹0.4431 crore and operating working capital ₹43.9385 crore come from the prospectus. Net IPO ₹47.5702 crore is credited once; ₹20 crore planned debt repayment reduces both cash and debt once. Actual deployment is a forecast bridge, not a verified utilization claim.

Project spending is ₹25.5083 crore, allocated 70% and 30% in years one and two. Growth capex is the larger of that project schedule and positive incremental revenue divided by assumed fixed-asset turnover; these overlapping needs are not added twice. Maintenance capex equals depreciation. Depreciation includes historical ₹4.8847 crore plus a ten-year life assumption for new assets.

Opening operating working capital is inventories ₹18.2812 crore plus receivables ₹21.4377 crore, short advances ₹3.8802 crore and other current assets ₹5.0391 crore, less payables ₹3.6414 crore and other current liabilities ₹1.0583 crore. Short provisions are excluded because cash tax is modeled separately; this differs from the prospectus broader ₹41.854 crore measure. Working capital is a stock. Annual cash use equals forecast stock minus the actual preceding stock, including the first year. The ₹2.0619 crore GCP allocation is reserved as a conservative cash use in year one; it is not credited as an additional asset or deducted again from EBIT.

Interest uses opening debt, half-year scheduled repayment and half-year new borrowing, with the financing circularity solved iteratively. Cash tax is 25.17% of positive PBT; no cash benefit is assumed for losses.

Existing proforma debt is amortized over five years as an analytical refinancing test, not an assertion of contractual maturities. Additional debt is limited to 30% of sales; remaining cash shortfalls require new equity at half the observed price. Neither financing source is guaranteed. A separate sensitivity immediately repays ₹10.878 crore of related demand debt.

Cash must cover a 5%-of-sales operating reserve. No dividends are assumed. Terminal enterprise value is EBIT times the exit EV/EBIT assumption; bank debt is subtracted, only cash above the operating reserve is added, and equity is divided by modeled diluted shares. IRR equals (terminal price / ₹133.75)^(1/5) minus one.

G3 is not failed merely because rescue funding is modeled in a severe scenario. The ordinary bear case and immediate demand-loan test are evaluated separately. If assumed rescue finance is unavailable in the severe case, curtailment or insolvency losses can be worse than the conditional dilution result.

Opening income-tax provision ₹1.1264 crore and accrued interest ₹0.0440 crore are conservatively settled before the first modeled year. Employee bonus/gratuity and expense provisions totaling ₹0.9141 crore are included in operating liabilities, reducing opening operating working capital to ₹43.0244 crore. Future-year taxes and interest are separate, so the opening claims are not duplicated.

central_case_basis.capacity: Prospectus pp 91 and 182: synthetic capacity increases from 3,750 to 5,000 MT, including 1,250 MT of finer-count yarn; polypropylene capacity remains 1,025 MT. FY26 production was 3,619 and 656 MT respectively.
central_case_basis.growth: An 8% revenue CAGR assumes approximately 5% annual synthetic volume growth plus approximately 3% realization/product-mix improvement, with services also expanding. Synthetic volume after five years is about 4,619 MT, below planned 5,000 MT capacity. This is a demand and commissioning assumption, not an order book or a claim of equal prices across yarns.
central_case_basis.margin: 17% EBIT margin is below FY26 22.31%, above FY25 12.48%. Disclosed solar power savings of ₹2.6028 crore support part of the improvement; remaining input/mix efficiency is only partly retained. Full FY25-margin reversion is separately stressed.
central_case_basis.multiple: 12× terminal EV/EBIT is an explicit valuation assumption, near the approximate 11.2× entry proforma EV/FY26 EBIT. It is not claimed as a measured peer median. The earlier 16× exit case required stronger growth and margin persistence and is retained separately, not silently erased.
central_case_basis.capacity_funding: The ₹25.5083 crore IPO machinery allocation is charged 70%/30% in the first two full operating years. Later incremental-capacity spending is linked to sales through an assumed 5× incremental fixed-asset turnover, with maintenance spending separately funded.
